classification.difficultyReason: Identify angle types from marked turns, including right, straight and full-turn symbols.

spec.description: Right-side vertex with upper-left and lower-left arms and an interior acute arc; plain endpoints, no dot.
spec.mathematics: The smaller opening is between 0 and 90 degrees. Coordinates reproduce qualitative appearance only; no numeric angle is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source arms and angle mark are visible; classification is in the answer.

answer.worked: The marked opening is less than $90^\circ$, so it is acute.

spec.description: Low central vertex with arms extending upper-left and slightly upper-right; broad arc above the vertex.
spec.mathematics: The upper interior opening is greater than 90 and less than 180 degrees; no exact measure is inferred.

answer.worked: The marked opening is greater than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$, so it is obtuse.

spec.description: Oblique straight line rising rightward, small central vertex dot and semicircle on the upper-left side.

answer.worked: The opposite arms form $180^\circ$, a straight line.

spec.description: Upper-right vertex, leftward horizontal arm, downward vertical arm and unfilled interior square.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular arms; square derived from both arm directions.
spec.answerVisibility: Given square remains visible; classification is answer-only.

answer.worked: The square marks $90^\circ$, a right angle.

spec.description: Right-side vertex and leftward arms; exterior arc passes below, right and above the vertex, leaving the small left opening unmarked.
spec.mathematics: The marked exterior sector is greater than 180 and less than 360 degrees. Arc winding selects the exterior sector without a directional arrow.

answer.worked: The marked exterior turn is greater than $180^\circ$ and less than $360^\circ$, so it is reflex.

spec.description: Leftward horizontal arm and steep upper-right arm with interior arc above-left of the vertex.
spec.mathematics: The marked opening lies between 90 and 180 degrees; no exact angle is given.

answer.worked: The marked opening is greater than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$, so it is obtuse.

spec.description: Rightward and downward arms; exterior arc runs through the upper and left regions. No square or numeric label.
spec.mathematics: The exterior arc selects the reflex turn. No additional right-angle marker or measure is introduced.

answer.worked: The exterior arc marks a turn greater than $180^\circ$ and less than $360^\circ$, so it is reflex.

spec.description: Lower-left vertex with upward and rightward arms and an unfilled square in the upper-right opening.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular arms; square derived from the arm directions.
spec.answerVisibility: Given square remains visible; classification is answer-only.

answer.worked: The square marks $90^\circ$, a right angle.

spec.description: Two close leftward, upward arms meet at a right-side vertex. An almost-complete exterior arc excludes the narrow opening.
spec.mathematics: The exterior sector exceeds 180 and is less than 360 degrees; the narrow interior sector is not the requested angle.

answer.worked: The almost-complete exterior turn is greater than $180^\circ$ and less than $360^\circ$, so it is reflex.

spec.description: Arm extends left and slightly down; second extends steeply lower-right. Exterior arc passes around the right and top to the left arm.
spec.mathematics: The marked larger sector lies between 180 and 360 degrees.

answer.worked: The marked exterior turn is greater than $180^\circ$ and less than $360^\circ$, so it is reflex.

spec.description: Horizontal straight line with central dot and semicircle below the line.

answer.worked: The opposite arms form $180^\circ$, a straight line.

spec.description: Central vertex dot, one upper-right arm and a complete circular turn marker.
spec.mathematics: The complete circle denotes a full 360-degree turn.
spec.answerVisibility: No numeric measure or classification is added to the question diagram.

answer.worked: The complete circle marks $360^\circ$, one revolution.
